### Headline summary
- Hackers breached USDA and FBI systems while exploiting critical flaws in VMware, Cisco, and Apache software. ([The Guardian Cybercrime](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/21/usda-fbi-outages-cyber-attack), [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/fbi-reportedly-hacked-again-this-time-targeting-nationwide-police-database/), [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/hackers-exploit-critical-vmware-cisco.html))
- F5 released emergency patches for six critical BIG-IP vulnerabilities that allow remote code execution. ([CSO Online](https://www.csoonline.com/article/4251711/f5-scrambles-to-fix-more-critical-big-ip-security-flaws-2.html), [Cyber Security News (FeedBurner)](https://cybersecuritynews.com/critical-f5-big-ip-vulnerabilities/))
- Suspected China-linked actors used AI agents to exploit a zero-day in medical imaging software to gain root access. ([The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/attackers-ai-agents-found-zero-day-in.html), [SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/amazon-china-linked-hackers-ai-agents-exploited-medical-software-zero-day/))

### USDA and FBI systems breached by hackers
Reports indicate that hackers breached the USDA's farmer-payment system and the FBI's National Crime Information Center, marking the second reported intrusion into FBI systems in two months. ([The Guardian Cybercrime](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/21/usda-fbi-outages-cyber-attack), [BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/fbi-reportedly-hacked-again-this-time-targeting-nationwide-police-database/))

### Hackers Exploit Critical VMware, Cisco, and Apache Flaws as Espionage Attacks Emerge
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Friday added four flaws impacting Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver, and Broadcom VMware vCenter to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV), citing evidence of active exploitation. ([The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/hackers-exploit-critical-vmware-cisco.html))

### F5 releases emergency fixes for critical BIG-IP vulnerabilities
F5 released out-of-band patches for six critical vulnerabilities in BIG-IP Access Policy Manager and iRules that could allow remote attackers to disrupt websites and execute malicious code. ([CSO Online](https://www.csoonline.com/article/4251711/f5-scrambles-to-fix-more-critical-big-ip-security-flaws-2.html), [Cyber Security News (FeedBurner)](https://cybersecuritynews.com/critical-f5-big-ip-vulnerabilities/))

### AI agents exploit zero-day in medical imaging software
Suspected China-linked hackers used autonomous AI agents to discover and exploit a previously unknown zero-day vulnerability in MONAI Label medical imaging software, gaining root access. ([The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/attackers-ai-agents-found-zero-day-in.html), [SecurityWeek](https://www.securityweek.com/amazon-china-linked-hackers-ai-agents-exploited-medical-software-zero-day/))

### Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw exploited to steal tenant data
Microsoft is warning organizations that it suffered a data breach after attackers exploited a vulnerability in its Entra Connect Health service to gain unauthorized access to administrator email addresses and tenant configuration information. ([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/microsoft-entra-connect-health-flaw-exploited-to-steal-tenant-data/))

### GL.iNet Says Attackers Used Its Cloud Service to Plant Malware on Routers and KVMs
GL.iNet, maker of the small travel routers many people use to run a VPN away from home, says an attacker used a hole in its cloud remote-management service to install malicious software on some of its routers and remote KVM devices. The company says it found the flaw on 20 November and closed it on… ([Privacy Affairs](https://www.privacyaffairs.com/glinet-security-incident/))

### GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG. The GnuPG project warned yesterday that the flaw could be used to steal data from affected applications and has released fixed versions. ([The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/gnupg-warns-critical-gpgme-flaw-could.html))

### PHP2Shell aftershock: 18 more PHP flaws put enterprise web admins on alert
PHP continues to root out flaws in its architecture, this week releasing fixes for a slew of additional security issues in the wake of PHP2Shell. The patches address 18 vulnerabilities , including a critical request smuggling flaw that could allow unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute code… ([CSO Online](https://www.csoonline.com/article/4251713/php2shell-aftershock-18-more-php-flaws-put-enterprise-web-admins-on-alert.html))
